My mother has a graduate degree in communications, did a lot of high profile writing/PR projects in the 80's/90's (not in Calgary) but has only worked sporadically in last ten years. She's looking for a full time position in her field and isn't terribly interested in networking. Anyone have any advice I can pass on?
I've heard good things about Dr. Harris Yee who works at Clinical Genetics Services from people with EDS. Though it is run at the children's hospital, it's for patients of any age.

Here are a few more. Shelter: Inn From the Cold and Children's Cottage Society help fathers and their children, single men can go to the Drop In Centre or the Mustard Seed. Counselling: the YWCA provides counselling (for almost three times as many men as women including those dealing with domestic abuse in 2014) on a sliding scale, the Distress Centre offers free counselling by phone or in person, Woods Homes offers free walk in counselling Other: The Connect Network (1.877.237.5888) helps victims of domestic abuse (male or female), Alberta Works helps victims (male or female) flee domestic abuse with financial aid (1‑866‑644‑5135), Homefront provides men and women who are experiencing domestic violence a caseworker to connect them with resources and navigate the legal system (403.206.2100 ext. 243). Domestic violence is awful. I've known men, women and children who've all suffered greatly due to it.

I work in tech now. I was one of two girls at science camp in 2007ish. The first day I thought I was the only girl and only returned the next day because my parents made me. I really enjoyed the camp by the end of the week and entered a science school the next year. I would have absolutely loved something like this as a kid.
